guest.service: The stock Go toolchain targeting wasip1 instead of a forked runtime or rewritten source, so new Go releases keep working. Cost: no cgo, so libraries such as go-sqlite3 cannot run, and mmap or flock code needs a stand-in.
host.sched: Preempts a node after 4,194,304 counted calls instead of by elapsed time, because a count replays identically. Cost: loops with no calls are never interrupted unless preempt.loops is on, which slows the guest, so it is off by default.
host.disk: A simulated disk with an explicit durability model instead of the real file system, so a crash keeps only fsynced data and strict POSIX cases can be tested. Cost: it tests a model, not the real kernel; XFS has none.
host.check: Histories are checked against a sequential model with Porcupine instead of single-result assertions, because concurrent operations must look as if they ran one at a time. Cost: checking is NP-complete, so a seed is abandoned after 30 s.
